1.explanation: All of these files live in the v2 report layer and collectively cover the generation, DOM construction, formatting, and high-level rendering pathways for the report. report-generator-test.js verifies the top-level HTML output, report-renderer-test.js drives the integration of all sections (including any added banner), dom-test.js ensures the correct DOM node creation for alerts, format-helpers-test.js covers any string formatting (including link injection), and category-renderer-test.js confirms categories render in the proper order relative to the banner. Updating these will allow you to add, style, and test the new Headless Chrome warning at the top of the report.
1.bug_scenario: The bug scenario appears at the top of a Lighthouse report generated by Headless Chrome. The screenshot shows the four circle‐style score badges (Progressive Web App, Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices) followed by a full‐width, red warning banner: “Note: Your site’s mobile performance may be worse than the numbers presented in this report. Lighthouse could not test on a mobile connection because Headless Chrome does not support network throttling. See crbug.com/728451.” The warning includes a yellow ⚠️ icon, red text, and a hyperlink. It sits above the first category section (“Progressive Web App”).
